topics.title: Cryptogamic Botany
topics.detail: 1. Cryptogamic Botany: Algae: Classification (Fritsch, Bold & Wynne), Major algal groups (Cyanophyta, Chlorophyta, Charophyta, Bacillariophyta, Phaeophyta, Rhodophyta), thallus organization, pigments, reserve food, life cycles (Isomorphic, Heteromorphic, Diplontic, Triphasic). Economic importance (agar, alginate, biofertilizers). Algal blooms. Fungi: Classification (Ainsworth), Major fungal groups (Phycomycetes, Ascomycetes, Basidiomycetes, Deuteromycetes), cell wall, hyphal modifications, reproduction. Lichens; mycorrhizae (Ectomycorrhizae vs Endomycorrhizae). Plant diseases & control. Bryophytes: Liverworts, Hornworts, Mosses – comparative study. Alternation of generations, apogamy, apospory.

topics.title: Pteridophytes & Gymnosperms
topics.detail: 2. Pteridophytes & Gymnosperms: Pteridophytes: Psilopsida, Lycopsida, Sphenopsida, Pteropsida. Heterospory & seed habit. Gymnosperms: Cycadales, Ginkgoales, Coniferales, and Gnetales– their structure, life history, affinities. Seed structure & ontogeny. Economic importance.

topics.title: Plant Anatomy & Embryology
topics.detail: 3. Plant Anatomy & Embryology: Anatomy: Meristems (apical meristems and the tunica-corpus theory). Tissue systems. Vascular cambium & secondary growth (dicot stem/root). Anomalous secondary growth. Leaf, stem, root anatomy. Embryology: Microsporogenesis, Megasporogenesis. Anther & ovule types. Pollination, fertilization, double fertilization. Embryo & endosperm development. Polyembryony, apomixis.

topics.title: Taxonomy of Angiosperms
topics.detail: 4. Taxonomy of Angiosperms: Systematics: Bentham & Hooker, Engler & Prantl, Takhtajan, Cronquist, APG. ICBN/ICN rules. Taxonomic hierarchy. Herbarium & botanical gardens. Modern Trends: Biosystematics, Chemotaxonomy, Numerical Taxonomy, Molecular Taxonomy. Families: Fabaceae, Solanaceae, Poaceae, Asteraceae, Liliaceae–their diagnostic characters and economic importance.

topics.title: Plant Physiology & Biochemistry
topics.detail: 5. Plant Physiology & Biochemistry: Water relations: Water potential (Ψw = Ψs + Ψp + Ψg) and its components; water absorption; transpiration; and stomatal regulation. Phloem transport (Pressure-Flow Hypothesis). Mineral Nutrition: Macro/micronutrients, deficiency symptoms, active/passive transport. Photosynthesis a n d respiration: Light-dependent reactions (Z-scheme), Calvin cycle, C3/C4/CAM/pathways, photorespiration, and celluar respiration including glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, the electron transport chain (ETC), and oxidative phosphorylation. Plant hormones: Auxins, gibberellins acids (GAs), cytokinins, abscisic acid (ABA), and ethylene. Photoperiodism, Vernalization, Dormancy, Germination.

topics.title: Ecology & Environmental Biology
topics.detail: 6. Ecology & Environmental Biology: Factors: Climatic (Light, Temperature, Wind), Edaphic (Soil), Biotic. Population & Community Ecology: Sampling (Quadrat, Line intercept), Ecological characteristics, Succession. Ecosystem ecology: Components, food chains, food webs, ecological pyramids, and biogeochemical cycles including t he hydrological (water) and the nitrogen cycle. Applied Ecology: Soil salinity & water logging in Pakistan – causes & reclamation. Deforestation, Biodiversity conservation, Pollution.

topics.detail: 2. Linear Data Structures: Arrays, linear lists, singly and doubly and circular linked lists, sorted lists, stacks, queues, deques and priority queue, and their practical applications such as bracket checking, expression conversion, and scheduling.

topics.title: Recursion and Sorting Algorithms
topics.detail: 3. Recursion and Sorting Algorithms: Direct recursion and recursive tracing and divide and conquer approaches, along with the discussion on different sorting algorithms like bubble sort, selection sort, insertion sort, merge sort, quick sort, heap sort, shell sort, radix sort and bucket sort.

topics.title: Searching and Hashing
topics.detail: 4. Searching and Hashing: Linear and binary search, hash functions, hash collision resolution, open addressing, chaining and indexing.

topics.title: Advanced Trees
topics.detail: 5. Advanced Trees: Binary tree, tree traversal, binary search tree (BST), balanced tree (AVL trees, M-way trees) and heaps.

topics.title: Graph and Advanced Applications
topics.detail: 6. Graph and Advanced Applications: Graph representations (Adjacency matrix and adjacency list), BFS, DFS, shortest path, minimum spanning trees, topological sort, cycle detection, graph coloring and data compression using Huffman coding.

topics.title: Introduction to Operating Systems and System Structures
topics.detail: 1. Introduction to Operating Systems and System Structures: History and Evolution, Classification of Operating Systems, System Components, System Services, Dual Mode Operation, Protection from Hardware/ Memory/ I/O, System Call Interface and Virtual Machines.

topics.title: Processes and Threads
topics.detail: 2. Processes and Threads: Concept of Processes, Process Control Block, States of Process, Process Scheduling, Process Creation and Process Termination (fork(), wait(), exec()), Multi-Threading Models, Threading Issues and Thread Libraries (Pthreads).

topics.title: CPU Scheduling
topics.detail: 3. CPU Scheduling: Criteria for Scheduling, Pre-Emptive and Non-Pre-Emptive Algorithms (FCFS, SJF, SRTF, Priority, Round Robin, MLQ, MLFQ), Thread Scheduling, Multiprocessor Scheduling.

topics.title: Process Synchronization and Concurrency
topics.detail: 4. Process Synchronization and Concurrency: Race Condition, Critical Section Problem, Software & Hardware Solutions to critical section problem (Peterson’s Solution and Test-and-Set lock), Mutex Locks, Semaphores, Classical Problems in Synchronization (Producer – Consumer Problem, Dining Philosophers Problem, Reader – Writer Problem) Monitors.

topics.title: Deadlock
topics.detail: 5. Deadlock: System Model, Deadlock Characteristics, Four Necessary Conditions of Deadlock, Resource Allocation Graphs, Deadlock Prevention & Avoidance (Banker’s Algorithm), Deadlock Detection & Recovery.

topics.title: Memory Management
topics.detail: 6. Memory Management: Address Binding, Logical Addresses vs Physical Addresses, Contiguous Memory Allocation (Text Segment, Data Segment, Heap Segment, MFT, MVT; Fragmentation), Paging, Page Tables and Hierarchical Inverted Page Tables, Segmentation and Paged Segmentation.

topics.title: Virtual Memory
topics.detail: 7. Virtual Memory: Demand Paging, Performance of Virtual Memory, Page Replacement Algorithms (FIFO, OPTIMAL, LRU, LFU), Frame Allocation, Thrashing, Working Set Model, Memory Mapped Files.

topics.title: Storage Management, File Systems and Security
topics.detail: 8. Storage Management, File Systems and Security: File Concept, Access Methods, Directory Structure and Disk Structure, Free-Space Management, Disk Scheduling Algorithms, RAIDs, File System Reliability and Protection, Security of Operating System.

topics.title: Number Systems and Binary Arithmetic
topics.detail: 1. Number Systems and Binary Arithmetic: Numerical representation, number system conversions, data representations, Radix and Diminished Radix Complements and Binary Subtraction.

topics.title: Boolean Algebra and Reduction of Boolean Functions
topics.detail: 2. Boolean Algebra and Reduction of Boolean Functions: Basic theorems and properties of Boolean algebra, Boolean functions, standard forms (canonical forms) (minterms and maxterms), reduction of Boolean functions (K-maps and QuineMcCluskey method).

topics.title: Combinational Logic Circuits
topics.detail: 3. Combinational Logic Circuits: Design and analysis techniques, design of combinational circuits (using gates), adders, subtractors, converters, magnitude comparators, decoders, encoders, multiplexers and demultiplexers.

topics.title: Sequential Logic Circuits
topics.detail: 4. Sequential Logic Circuits: Latches, Flip-Flops (SR, D, JK, T), Analysis of clocked sequential circuits, State reduction and assignment, registers and Shift Registers.

topics.title: Synchronous and Asynchronous State Machines
topics.detail: 5. Synchronous and Asynchronous State Machines: Ripple and synchronous counters, timing sequences, Mealy and Moore Finite State Machines.

topics.title: Memory Units and Programmable Logic Devices
topics.detail: 6. Memory Units and Programmable Logic Devices: Random Access Memory (RAM), Read Only Memory (ROM), Programmable Logic Arrays (PLA’s), CPLDs, FPGAs, logic families and digital integrated circuits.

topics.title: Hardware Description Languages and Circuit Simulations
topics.detail: 7. Hardware Description Languages and Circuit Simulations: Overview of hardware description language (Verilog HDL/VHDL) and electronic design automation tools for digital logic simulation (MultiSim, SPICE or similar).

topics.title: Requirements Engineering

topics.title: Analysis and Modeling (structured and object-oriented)

topics.title: Architectural and Component Level Design

topics.title: Software Verification, Validation and Testing

topics.title: Project Management and Evolution

topics.title: Data Models and E-R Modeling

topics.title: Relational Model and Relational Algebra

topics.title: SQL

topics.title: Database Design and Normalization

topics.title: Physical Storage and Indexing
topics.detail: 6. Physical Storage and Indexing: Storage structure, file organization, indexed files, hashed files, B-tree structure, dense and sparse indices, and database tuning.

topics.title: Transactions, Concurrency Control, and Database Recovery
topics.detail: 7. Transactions, Concurrency Control, and Database Recovery: Atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability, transaction processing, concurrency control using locking, two phase locking, timestamps and optimistic concurrency control, deadlock and database recovery mechanisms.

topics.title: Advanced and Emerging Databases

topics.title: Symbolic Mathematics and Probabilistic Reasoning

topics.title: Neural Networks and Deep Learning

topics.title: The Theory of Consumer Behaviour

Price- consumption and Demand curve. Income and Substitution effects of a price change, the Hicksian method and the Slutsky method. Identification of normal goods, inferior goods and Giffen goods.

topics.title: The Theory of Production

The very long run and the endogenous technical change.

topics.title: Aggregate Demand and Aggregate Supply

topics.title: Inflation and Unemployment

Hysteresis and the natural rate hypotheses.

topics.title: Consumption Theories and Their Implications
topics.detail: 8. Consumption Theories and Their Implications: Keynesian absolute income hypothesis, Simon Kuznets findings, Duesenbury‟s hypothesis, Permanent income hypothesis, life cycle hypothesis, Robert Hall and the random-walk hypothesis.

topics.title: Solid state and X-rays
topics.detail: C. Solid state and X-rays: Crystalline structure and properties; production of X-rays and crystal-structure applications; heat capacities of solids.

topics.title: Electrochemistry

topics.title: Thermochemistry and kinetics
topics.detail: E. Thermochemistry and kinetics: Heat of reaction, basic chemical equilibrium and factors affecting reaction rate.

topics.title: Industrial chemistry
topics.detail: F. Industrial chemistry: Corrosion mechanisms and control; water hardness and treatment; fuels and combustion; lubricants; cement chemistry; environmental chemistry, chemical hazards and safety.

topics.title: Basic analytical methods
topics.detail: G. Basic analytical methods: Titrimetry, spectrophotometry and chromatography: principles and interpretation at introductory level.

topics.title: Circuit fundamentals

topics.detail: B. topics.title: Descriptive Statistics
topics.detail: 1. Descriptive Statistics: Meaning of Statistics, its characteristics, uses and misuses of statistics, observations and variables, types of variables, data and its types according to nature (qualitative and quantitative), w.r.t. source (primary and secondary), measurement scales (nominal, ordinal, interval and ratio), population and sample, descriptive and inferential statistics, description of qualitative and quantitative data using frequency tables and graphs (simple bar chart, histogram, pie chart, stem and leaf plot), measures of central tendency and their types. Ungrouped and Grouped Data: arithmetic mean, median and mode, empirical relationship among mean, median and mode, properties of arithmetic mean (proof not required), weighted mean and its application. Ungrouped Data: Geometric mean and harmonic mean, Quantiles (quartiles, deciles and percentiles), relative merits and demerits of all above averages, measure of dispersion, absolute and relative measure of dispersion: Range, semi-interquartile range, variance and standard deviation, properties of variance and standard deviation (proof not required), coefficient of quartile deviation, coefficient of variation, Box and whisker plot, standardized variables.

topics.title: Concept of probability and Random variables
topics.detail: 2. Concept of probability and Random variables: Random experiment, sample space and events, counting principles, including the multiplication principle, combinations, and permutations, introduction to probability and axioms of probability, basic laws of probability, addition and multiplication laws of probability for two events, conditional probabilities, Bayes’ theorem (proof not required) and its application, discrete random variable, probability mass function and cumulative distribution function, joint distribution of two discrete random variables, marginal and conditional distribution, continuous random variable, probability density function and cumulative distribution function, joint distribution of two continuous random variables, marginal and conditional distribution, mathematical expectations and its properties, mean, variance, covariance and correlation of two discrete and continuous random variables.

topics.title: Probability Distributions
topics.detail: 3. Probability Distributions: Discrete Binomial, hypergeometric, Poisson distribution, application and fitting to real life data, concept of negative binomial and geometric distribution, continuous exponential and normal distributions, applications and fitting to real-life data, properties of normal distribution.

topics.title: Regression and Correlation Analysis
topics.detail: 4. Regression and Correlation Analysis: Concept of regression and correlation analysis, scatter diagram and its uses, estimation of simple linear regression, properties of the least-squares regression line, standard error of estimate, coefficient of determination, linear correlation, coefficient of correlation and its properties. Spearman’s rank correlation (with and without tied observations), partial and multiple correlations up to three variables.

topics.title: Index Numbers and Basics of Time series
topics.detail: 5. Index Numbers and Basics of Time series: Construction and application of wholesale price index numbers, fixed and chain base methods, weighted index numbers (Laspeyres’, Paasche’s, Fisher’s ideal and Marshall-Edgeworth indices), tests for the consistency of Index Numbers, construction of consumer price index numbers, sensitive price indicator, components of a time series, analysis of time series, measurement of secular trend and seasonal variations by various methods, deseasonalization of data.

topics.title: Sampling and Sampling Distribution
topics.detail: 6 Sampling and Sampling Distribution: Concept of sampling, advantages and scope of sampling, probability and non probability sampling, sampling and non sampling error, sampling design and sampling frame, sampling design of simple random sampling, stratified, systematic and cluster sampling, judgment and quota sampling, sampling distributions of sample means, proportions and variances under simple random sampling, sampling distributions of mean of stratified random sampling, sampling distributions of difference between two sample means and the sample proportions, and their properties, concept of central limit theorem, concepts of t-, 𝜒 2 -, F-distributions.

topics.title: Estimation and Testing of Hypothesis
topics.detail: 7 Estimation and Testing of Hypothesis: Estimates and estimators, point estimator and its properties: Unbiasedness, consistency, efficiency and sufficiency, interval estimation and its interpretations, interval estimation of the single population mean or proportion with known and unknown variances, differences between two mean/proportions with known and unknown variances, determination of sample size, interval estimation of population variance and ratio of two population variances, null and alternative hypothesis, simple and composite hypothesis, concept of Type-I and Type-II error, level of significance, concept of p-value, acceptance and rejection regions, one sided and two sided test, testing of hypothesis for single mean/proportion, difference between two means/proportions, testing of hypothesis (based on small sample and unknown population variance) for single mean, difference between two means, paired and independent observations, testing of hypothesis about the variances and equality of two variances, concept of association, contingency tables, chi-square test for independence of attributes.

topics.title: Analysis of variance and Experimental Design
topics.detail: 8 Analysis of variance and Experimental Design: Definition, importance and assumptions of analysis of variance, partitioning of sums of squares and degrees of freedom in one and two way classification, testing the equality of means for one and two way classification, multiple comparison tests: least significant difference test, Duncan’s multiple range test, principles of experimental design, completely randomized, randomized complete block and Latin square design, description of the layout, and statistical analysis, advantages and disadvantages of each design.

topics.title: Non-Parametric Tests
topics.detail: 9 Non-Parametric Tests: Parametric vs Non-parametric tests, when to use non-parametric procedures, testing procedures and applications one-sample tests: Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test, Run test, testing procedures and applications two related-sample tests: Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test, testing procedures and applications for two independent samples: Mann-Whitney U test, run test, testing procedures and application two or more independent samples: Kruskal Wallis H test.

topics.title: Vital Statistics and Official Statistics

topics.title: APPLIED BASIC VETERINARY SCIENCES Applied anatomy and physiology
topics.detail: 1. APPLIED BASIC VETERINARY SCIENCES Applied anatomy and physiology: Functional organisation of the digestive, respiratory, cardiovascular, urinary, reproductive, endocrine, nervous and musculoskeletal systems; skin, udder and lactation. Relevant differences among ruminants, equines, companion animals and poultry, with applications to health and production. Applied biochemistry: Principles of nutrient metabolism, energy balance, fluid and electrolyte balance and acid–base regulation; their relevance to nutritional, metabolic and clinical disorders. General pathology: Cell injury, inflammation, degeneration, necrosis, circulatory disturbances, tissue repair and neoplasia; interpretation of these processes in common animal diseases. Necropsy and interpretation of common gross lesions. Microbiology, immunology and parasitology: Characteristics of bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites relevant to disease transmission and control. Host–pathogen relationships, innate and acquired immunity, maternal immunity, vaccination and immunosuppression. Application of parasite life cycles to prevention and control.

topics.title: CLINICAL MEDICINE, DIAGNOSTICS AND PRIORITY ANIMAL DISEASES Clinical assessment
topics.detail: 2. CLINICAL MEDICINE, DIAGNOSTICS AND PRIORITY ANIMAL DISEASES Clinical assessment: History taking, systematic clinical examination, identification of problems, differential diagnosis and clinical decision making. Recognition of emergencies. Diagnostic approaches: Selection, collection, preservation and transportation of specimens. Interpretation of basic hematology, serum biochemistry, urinalysis, fecal examination, cytology, microscopy, microbial culture, antimicrobial susceptibility reports, serology and molecular tests. Principles, indications and limitations of radiography and ultrasonography. Priority livestock infectious diseases: Foot-and-mouth disease, haemorrhagic septicemia, blackleg, anthrax, peste des petits ruminants, lumpy skin disease, bovine ephemeral fever, brucellosis, bovine tuberculosis and rabies. Priority poultry infectious diseases: Newcastle disease, avian influenza, infectious bursal disease, infectious bronchitis, Marek’s disease, salmonellosis and colibacillosis. Parasitic and vector-borne diseases: Tick infestations, theileriosis, babesiosis, anaplasmosis, trypanosomiasis, gastrointestinal helminthiasis, fasciolosis, coccidiosis, mange and other common ectoparasite infestations; practical control strategies. Common clinical and production disorders: Mastitis, neonatal diarrhoea, pneumonia, bloat, ruminal acidosis, displaced abomasum, hypocalcaemia, ketosis, pregnancy toxemia and lameness. Recognition, diagnostic approach, management principles and prevention of production losses. Representative fungal diseases: dermatophytosis and aspergillosis; recognition, diagnostic approach, management principles and prevention. Companion and working animals: canine parvovirus infection, canine distemper, feline panleukopenia, equine colic, strangles, glanders and equine piroplasmosis. Preventive healthcare of companion animals, working equids and camels.

topics.title: VETERINARY SURGERY, ANESTHESIA, REPRODUCTION AND OBSTETRICS Surgical principles
topics.detail: 3. VETERINARY SURGERY, ANESTHESIA, REPRODUCTION AND OBSTETRICS Surgical principles: Animal handling and restraint; asepsis, sterilisation, wound assessment, wound healing and surgical infection prevention. Indications and welfare considerations for common procedures, including castration, dehorning, hernia repair and management of hoof conditions. Anesthesia and emergency care: Principles of local and general anesthesia, analgesia and perioperative monitoring. Initial assessment and stabilisation of shock, hemorrhage, traumatic injuries and fractures; postoperative care; principles of fluid and electrolyte therapy; recognition of dehydration and acid–base disturbances. Reproductive management: Estrous cycles, estrus detection, breeding timing, artificial insemination, semen quality and handling, breeding soundness examination of males, pregnancy diagnosis and reproductive records. Interpretation of conception rate, services per conception and calving interval. Infertility and reproductive disorders: Anestrus, repeat breeding, reproductive infections, abortion and common postpartum disorders; diagnostic approach, prevention and herd-level management. Obstetrics and neonatal care: Recognition and management principles of dystocia, retained fetal membranes, metritis and uterine or vaginal prolapse. Parturition management, colostrum provision and prevention of neonatal losses.

topics.title: EPIDEMIOLOGY, HERD HEALTH AND BIOSECURITY Epidemiological principles
topics.detail: 4. EPIDEMIOLOGY, HERD HEALTH AND BIOSECURITY Epidemiological principles: Disease occurrence and distribution; incidence, prevalence, morbidity, mortality, case fatality and attack rate. Risk factors, association and causation; transmission patterns and population susceptibility. Research and evidence interpretation: Principles of sampling, observational studies and clinical trials. Basic descriptive statistics, bias, confounding and uncertainty. Interpretation of simple tables, graphs and study findings. Interpretation of relative risk, odds ratios and confidence intervals using simple supplied data; statistical significance and practical importance. Diagnostic performance: Sensitivity, specificity and predictive values; interpretation of screening and confirmatory tests. Surveillance and outbreak investigation: Passive, active and sentinel surveillance; case definitions, line lists, time–place–animal analysis, specimen selection, source tracing and disease reporting. Early warning, disease mapping and risk-based surveillance. Herd and flock health programs: Vaccination strategies, vaccine cold chains, assessment of vaccination failure, quarantine, isolation, cleaning, disinfection, movement management and farm biosecurity.

topics.title: VETERINARY PHARMACOLOGY, TOXICOLOGY AND ANTIMICROBIAL STEWARDSHIP Rational therapeutics
topics.detail: 5. VETERINARY PHARMACOLOGY, TOXICOLOGY AND ANTIMICROBIAL STEWARDSHIP Rational therapeutics: Applied pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics; selection of drug class, route and regimen according to clinical indication. Contraindications, interactions, adverse effects and assessment of treatment response. Principles of antimicrobial, antiparasitic, anti-inflammatory, analgesic and supportive therapy. Prescription quality, storage, product quality, treatment records and pharmacovigilance. Antimicrobial resistance and stewardship: Selection and transmission of resistance among animals, humans and the environment; consequences for animal health, public health and food production. Culture and susceptibility testing, empirical versus targeted treatment; antimicrobial selection and duration; distinctions among treatment, metaphylaxis and prophylaxis. Protection of critically important antimicrobials and monitoring of antimicrobial use. Drug residue prevention: Withdrawal periods, maximum residue limits and prevention of veterinary-drug residues in milk, meat and eggs. Veterinary toxicology: Cyanide, nitrate or nitrite, urea, pesticides, mycotoxins, heavy metals and poisonous plants. Recognition, diagnostic approach, immediate response, principles of antidotal and supportive treatment and prevention.

topics.title: VETERINARY PUBLIC HEALTH, ONE HEALTH AND FOOD SAFETY One Health
topics.detail: 6. VETERINARY PUBLIC HEALTH, ONE HEALTH AND FOOD SAFETY One Health: Relationships among human, animal, plant and environmental health. Joint surveillance, information sharing, coordinated risk assessment and prevention at the livestock–wildlife–human interface. Institutional coordination, community participation and preparedness for zoonotic outbreaks. Priority zoonoses: Rabies, brucellosis, bovine tuberculosis, anthrax, leptospirosis, Q fever, salmonellosis, campylobacteriosis, echinococcosis, toxoplasmosis and Crimean–Congo haemorrhagic fever. Reservoirs, exposure routes, occupational risks and coordinated prevention. Milk and animal-source food hygiene: Hygienic production, collection, processing, storage and transportation of milk, meat, eggs and fish. Pasteurization, cold-chain management and prevention of contamination and adulteration. Meat inspection and slaughter hygiene: Objectives and principles of ante-mortem and post-mortem inspection; slaughter hygiene, identification of public-health hazards and handling of condemned material. Food-safety management: Biological, chemical and physical hazards; antimicrobial residues, aflatoxins and other contaminants. Good hygiene practices, hazard analysis and critical control points (HACCP), traceability, sampling, recall and risk communication. Environmental and occupational safety: Safe handling of animals and specimens; personal protection, laboratory biosafety and biosecurity. Management of carcasses, manure, wastewater, sharps and veterinary waste.

topics.title: ANIMAL PRODUCTION, NUTRITION AND FARM MANAGEMENT Livestock production systems
topics.detail: 7. ANIMAL PRODUCTION, NUTRITION AND FARM MANAGEMENT Livestock production systems: Smallholder and commercial dairy, beef, sheep, goat and camel production systems. Locally important breeds, production constraints and opportunities for improvement. Housing and husbandry: Housing, ventilation, stocking density, water supply, sanitation and animal comfort. Calf and young-stock rearing, milking management, lactation and dry-period management; maintenance of working animals. Poultry production: Broiler, layer and breeder management; hatchery hygiene, incubation, hatchability, chick quality, brooding, lighting, litter management and ventilation. Performance assessment: Milk yield and quality, growth, mortality, culling, reproductive efficiency, feed conversion, egg production and flock uniformity. Use of farm records and benchmarks to identify and resolve management problems. Nutritional principles: Functions of energy, protein, fibre, minerals, vitamins and water; digestion and nutrient utilisation in ruminants, monogastric animals and poultry. Balanced feeding: Requirements for maintenance, growth, reproduction and production; body-condition assessment and recognition of nutritional deficiencies and excesses. Simple ration evaluation using supplied feed-composition and requirement data. Fodder and feed resources: Locally available feeds, pasture management, seasonal fodder planning, hay, silage, crop residues and safe use of non-conventional feeds. Feeding management: Feeding of young, transition and lactating animals and poultry; prevention of feeding-related disorders, drought feeding and water security. Feed safety and efficiency: Sampling, quality assessment, adulteration, spoilage, mycotoxins and storage losses. Safe use of supplements, urea and additives; principles of probiotics, prebiotics and feed enzymes. Reduction of feeding costs and nutrient losses while maintaining health and productivity. Aquaculture: Basic production systems, water quality, stocking, feeding, biosecurity and recognition of fish mortality events; food- safety implications and integrated production systems. Wildlife and zoo animals: Principles of conservation, captive-animal health, quarantine, welfare and disease risks at wildlife–livestock interfaces.

topics.title: ANIMAL GENETICS, BREEDING AND BIOTECHNOLOGY Genetic principles
topics.detail: 8. ANIMAL GENETICS, BREEDING AND BIOTECHNOLOGY Genetic principles: Inheritance, quantitative traits, heritability, selection, breeding values, inbreeding, crossbreeding and heterosis. Breeding programs: Performance and pedigree recording; selection of economically important traits. Breeding strategies suited to local production conditions; conservation of indigenous breeds, adaptability and disease resistance. Reproductive biotechnology: Estrus synchronization, semen cryopreservation, sexed semen, embryo transfer and in vitro embryo production. Diagnostic biotechnology: Applications and limitations of conventional polymerase chain reaction (PCR), reverse-transcription PCR, real-time PCR, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), rapid antigen tests, point-of- care diagnostics and genomic sequencing. Vaccines and emerging technologies: Principles and applications of conventional, recombinant, viral-vectored and nucleic-acid vaccines. Genomic selection and its practical applications. Awareness of emerging applications of gene editing, nanotechnology and targeted drug delivery.

topics.title: DIGITAL VETERINARY SERVICES, ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND PRECISION FARMING Digital services
topics.detail: 9. DIGITAL VETERINARY SERVICES, ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND PRECISION FARMING Digital services: Electronic clinical and farm records, animal identification, traceability, mobile disease reporting, geographic information systems (GIS) and tele-veterinary services. Precision livestock farming: Sensors and wearables for monitoring activity, estrus, rumination, temperature, milk quality and farm conditions. Artificial intelligence: Basic concepts of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning. Applications in diagnostic-image interpretation, disease surveillance, outbreak-risk prediction, production forecasting and clinical decision support. Generative AI applications in documentation, information retrieval and farmer communication; verification of outputs, factual errors and limitations of automated advice.

topics.title: LIVESTOCK ECONOMICS, POLICY, GOVERNANCE AND EXTENSION Sector development
topics.detail: 10. LIVESTOCK ECONOMICS, POLICY, GOVERNANCE AND EXTENSION Sector development: Contributions of livestock and poultry to livelihoods, nutrition, food security, employment and rural development; principal constraints and development priorities. Applied economics: Fixed and variable costs, farm budgets, gross margins, break- even analysis and partial budgeting. Simple cost–benefit and cost-effectiveness comparisons; economic losses from animal disease. Markets and value chains: Livestock and product marketing, quality incentives, producer organisations, credit, insurance, traceability and barriers to domestic and export market access. Policy and regulation: Objectives and implementation of frameworks concerning animal disease control, quarantine, veterinary medicines, feed quality, breeding, food safety and welfare. Veterinary certification and principles of sanitary trade requirements. Institutional coordination: Roles of provincial and federal services, local administration, laboratories, universities, professional regulators, private providers and international organisations. Veterinary service delivery and extension: Access in underserved areas, mobile services, referral networks, farmer education, participatory extension, public–private partnerships and entrepreneurship. Inclusion of women and smallholders; risk communication and management of misinformation. Program management and professional ethics: Needs assessment, priority setting, objectives, budgeting, implementation, monitoring and evaluation. Accountability, transparent resource allocation, informed consent, confidentiality, accurate certification and management of conflicts of interest. Planning and monitoring public vaccination campaigns; procurement and distribution of veterinary supplies, maintenance of essential stocks and equitable allocation of veterinary services.

topics.title: ANIMAL WELFARE, CLIMATE RESILIENCE AND DISASTER MANAGEMENT Welfare assessment
topics.detail: 11. ANIMAL WELFARE, CLIMATE RESILIENCE AND DISASTER MANAGEMENT Welfare assessment: Physical and behavioural indicators; nutrition, environment, health, behaviour and mental state. Prevention of avoidable pain, injury, fear and distress. Humane management: Welfare during housing, handling, transport, markets and slaughter; euthanasia principles. Welfare of companion, working, laboratory and captive wildlife animals; responsible ownership and humane population management. Ethical animal use: Principles of replacement, reduction and refinement in teaching and research. Climate resilience: Effects of heat stress, floods, drought and changing vector distributions on health and productivity. Sustainable production: Efficient resource use, manure management, reduction of greenhouse-gas emissions and nutrient losses, biodiversity conservation and sustainable pasture management. Disaster management: Risk assessment, contingency planning, evacuation, rescue, emergency shelter, feed and water provision, carcass disposal and continuity of veterinary services. Post-disaster surveillance, rehabilitation and coordination with disaster-management authorities.

topics.title: ANIMAL DIVERSITY (INVERTEBRATES) Introduction, taxonomy, general organization, structure and function, reproduction and…
topics.detail: 1. ANIMAL DIVERSITY (INVERTEBRATES) Introduction, taxonomy, general organization, structure and function, reproduction and life cycles, phylogenetic relationships, and economic importance of major invertebrate groups: Protozoa and Parazoa: Protozoa: Locomotion and types of pseudopodia, reproduction and parasitic protozoans. Porifera: Cellular organization, body wall, skeleton, and canal systems. Radiata, Triploblastic Acoelomates, and Pseudocoelomates: Cnidaria: Body wall, nematocysts, polymorphism, alternation of generations and coral reefs. Platyhelminthes: Body wall, parasitic adaptations, and life cycles of some major groups (e.g., Fasciola hepatica, Taeniasolium). Aschelminthes and Nematoda:Pseudocoelomate organization, body wall, and life cycles of human parasitic nematodes (e.g., Hookworms, Pinworms, filarial worms). Coelomate Invertebrates and Major Lineages: Mollusca: Modifications of foot, feeding mechanisms and predatory adaptations of cephalopods. Annelida &Arthropoda: Metamerism, tagmatization, mouthparts, ecdysis, metamorphosis, and ecological importance. Echinodermata: Diversity; water vascular system, larval forms and development.

topics.title: Animal Diversity (Vertebrates) Chordata
topics.detail: 2. Animal Diversity (Vertebrates) Chordata: Introduction and General Organization Origin, diagnostic characteristics and basic chordate body plan; major subdivisions of chordates, including proto-chordates and vertebrates. Fishes: Vertebrate Success in Water Origin, diversity, classification and phylogenetic relationships of major fish groups. Structural and functional adaptations for aquatic life: swim bladder; respiration; excretion and osmoregulation. Amphibians: The First Terrestrial Vertebrates Origin, classification and evolutionary relationships of amphibians. Structural, physiological and behavioral adaptations for aquatic and terrestrial life: Respiration, reproduction and development. Reptiles: The First Amniotes Evolution of reptiles, adaptations for terrestrial life, excretion, osmoregulation, reproduction and development; Extinction of dinosaurs; poisonous apparatus and biting mechanism of snakes. Aves: Feathers, Flight and Endothermy Evolutionary history and major adaptations associated with feathers, flight and endothermy. Structural and functional adaptations for aerial locomotion and respiration. Bird migration and navigation. Mammalia: Specialized Teeth, Hair, Endothermy and Viviparity Origin, diversity and emphasis on major mammalian groups. Dentition in vertebrates. Comparative account of the evolution of the heart and vertebrate stomach. Temperature regulation and endothermy.

topics.title: PRINCIPLES OF LIFE AND GENERAL ZOOLOGY Cell and Molecular Biology Comparative analysis of prokaryotic and eukaryotic…
topics.detail: 3. PRINCIPLES OF LIFE AND GENERAL ZOOLOGY Cell and Molecular Biology Comparative analysis of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells. Structure and specialized functions of the nucleus, plasma membrane and cytoplasmic organelles. Enzyme structure, catalytic mechanisms, regulation, and inhibition. Major metabolic pathways: glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, and the electron transport chain. DNA as genetic material, structural organization of nucleic acids, the genetic code, transcription, and translation. Mitosis and meiosis, and their biological significance. Animal Form, Function and General Physiology Vertebrate integument. Ultra-structure of muscle fibrils and mechanisms of muscle contraction. Regional functional organization of the gastrointestinal tract. Composition and functions of blood and internal fluids. Cardiovascular dynamics: electrical activity of the heart, cardiac output and blood pressure regulation. Comparative account of respiratory organs; properties and functions of respiratory pigments. Functional anatomy of the vertebrate nephron and urine formation. Mechanism of osmoregulation, and thermoregulation. Structural and functional units of the nervous system. Nerve impulse and its transmission. Structure and function of sensory organs (eye and ear). Endocrine glands, classes of hormones, mechanisms of hormone action. Genetics & Recombinant DNA Technology Mendelian principles of inheritance, gene interactions, multiple alleles, linkage, crossing over and sex-linked inheritance. Eukaryotic chromosome structure; chromosomal aberrations, gene mutations, and the evolving gene concept. Recombinant DNA technology, cloning strategies, applications of genetic engineering, and transgenic animals. Evolutionary Biology Theories of the origin of life. Darwinism and Neo-Darwinism. Causes of variation and types of natural selection. Genetic drift and Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. Species concepts, mechanisms of speciation (allopatric, parapatric, sympatric), adaptive radiation, phylogeny and ontogeny. Environmental Biology & Ecology Ecosystem concepts: components, primary/secondary productivity, trophic levels, food chains, food webs, and energy flow dynamics. Biogeochemical cycles (carbon, nitrogen). Environmental pollution (air, water, land), greenhouse effect, acid rain, global warming, climate change, and wildlife conservation and management.
